title: Lemon sandwich biscuits
subtitle: crisp, buttery shortbread rounds sandwiched with lemon curd
excerpt: Lemon sandwich biscuits are thin, crisp, buttery rounds sandwiched in pairs with lemon curd. The biscuit base is a simple egg-yolk shortbread that bakes pale and snaps clean. The lemon curd filling adds a sharp, creamy contrast to the butter biscuit. Use a thick, good-quality lemon curd for the best result; a thin curd makes the sandwiches difficult to handle.
sourceNotes: Sandwich biscuits filled with fruit curd are documented in British home baking from the nineteenth century onward. Lemon curd as a filling for sponge cakes and biscuits was popular in Victorian and Edwardian cookery.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Bake the biscuits up to 3 days ahead and store in an airtight tin. Sandwich with lemon curd on the day of serving; assembled sandwiches soften after a few hours.

content.text: Lemon sandwich biscuits are two thin, buttery biscuit rounds sandwiched with a generous layer of lemon curd. The biscuit base uses egg yolk rather than whole egg, which gives a shorter, more crumbly texture. The lemon curd should be thick and cold when you sandwich; a runny curd drips out on the first bite.

Sift together the flour and icing sugar. Rub in the cold butter until the mixture looks like fine breadcrumbs. Add the egg yolks, lemon zest, and vanilla extract and mix until the dough just comes together.
Press into a flat disc, wrap, and chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 160 degrees C (fan 140 degrees C / gas 3). Line two baking trays with baking paper.
Roll the dough to about 4 mm thick on a lightly floured surface. Cut into rounds about 5 cm in diameter. Place on the prepared trays and chill for 10 minutes before baking.
Bake for 12 to 14 minutes until just set and barely coloured. They will still look pale. Leave on the tray for 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack to cool completely.

Pair the cooled biscuits by size. Spread or pipe about a teaspoon of cold lemon curd onto the flat side of one biscuit from each pair. Press the second biscuit on top, flat side down, and press gently to bond without squeezing the filling out.

attrs.avoid: Avoid pressing too hard when sandwiching, especially with thinner biscuits.
attrs.fix: Apply lemon curd only to the centre of the biscuit base, leaving a small gap around the edge, so you can apply gentle central pressure without the biscuit snapping.

attrs.problem: Lemon curd oozing out of the sides
attrs.avoid: Avoid room temperature or warm lemon curd; it is too runny to stay in the sandwich.
attrs.fix: Use cold lemon curd straight from the fridge and use slightly less than you think you need. The filling spreads as you press the sandwich together.
